solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Helper seen around people following violent attack

indicators.note: something seen turned around is viewed from the other end, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: an aid is a thing that helps, like a hearing aid
a tribe is a people or clan

explanation.surface: An assistant gets caught up in a crowd after somebody launches a violent assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' places the people after the turned helper; the definition is the verbal kind of violent attack, a bitter tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a forceful, bitter verbal onslaught, so it is an attack in words rather than fists.

clue.text: The grammarian's name for it? Sure thing!

blocks.note: first meaning: the word 'The', which opens the clue, is what grammar books call this
second meaning, read literally: a certain item, an object you can be sure of

explanation.walkthrough: The clue's opening word is itself the thing being named; 'Sure thing!' sounds like casual agreement but splits into sure = definite and thing = article.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar labels 'the' this way, and an article is also an item, so a definite one is a certain object.

clue.text: A model upset Greek author, apparently

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means tipped up, so the word is written bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: A sitter for an artist gets upset with an ancient Greek writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' is there because historians doubt the fable-teller ever existed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the Greek fabulist credited with the fables, though his existence is uncertain.

clue.text: Decided on finished puzzle

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a puzzle finished is a puzzle solved

explanation.surface: Someone settled on a choice once the crossword was done.
explanation.definitionFit: To be resolved is to have made up one's mind firmly, a synonym for having decided.

clue.text: Skimpy underpants hiding the bottom

indicators.note: the bottom of a down entry is its final letter, and hiding it drops that letter

blocks.note: briefs are close-fitting underpants

explanation.surface: A scanty pair of knickers that barely covers the wearer's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's bottom is anatomical; cryptically it is the last letter of the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief means short or scanty, so skimpy clothing is brief in coverage.

clue.text: What top plainclothes copper did is rotten

blocks.note: what the top person in a department does is run it
the Criminal Investigation Department, the branch of British police whose detectives wear plain clothes

explanation.surface: A senior detective's conduct is condemned as corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'what the top plain-clothes copper did': he ran the CID, the detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid describes food gone off and foul-smelling, so it is a synonym for rotten.

clue.text: An alto struggling to describe music such as Schoenberg's?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; 'to describe' tells you it qualifies this music

indicators.note: a singer struggling is in disorder, so the letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A choir singer finds a modernist score hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: an alto would struggle with keyless music.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoenberg pioneered music written without a home key, which is what atonal means.

clue.text: A neurotic ordered a stiff drink

indicators.note: ordered means put into an arrangement, so these letters are sorted afresh

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: An anxious person asks for something strong to steady the nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a strong French orange liqueur, an example of a stiff alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Senior member of staff noted career girl required training

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so these letters must be drilled into a new formation

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A well-known ambitious young woman had to be trained before joining the senior staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A director-general is the chief executive of an organisation such as the BBC, its most senior official.

clue.text: One very tall European runner, say, is ahead

indicators.note: being ahead in a down entry means sitting above, so the vegetable comes first

blocks.note: a runner bean is one kind of bean, as 'say' signals
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A lanky continental athlete takes the lead in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete beside the European, but it is the climbing vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Beanpole is informal for a very tall, thin person, from the tall stakes beans climb.

clue.text: Unintelligent type helping Turner in the kitchen

blocks.note: fish are proverbially brainless, and a fish is slang for a dupe or poor player
a slice is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: A dim-witted person lends the chef a hand by flipping food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like a person or the painter; it is a kitchen tool that turns food in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish slice is a broad slotted spatula used for turning and lifting food when cooking.

clue.text: Topless seller of tights?—It's Twiggy!

definitions.note: read as 'it is twiggy', the thing described; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter is taken away

blocks.note: a hosier sells stockings, socks and tights

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about a famous 1960s model posing topless for a hosiery firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Twiggy was a famous 1960s model; here the word means made of twigs.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow whose long pliant shoots are used in basketry, so it is twiggy.

clue.text: North-eastern China is land with no coast

blocks.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
E is the compass abbreviation for east
Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so china means a pal

explanation.surface: A geography statement that north-eastern China is inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, which only strengthens the geographical surface; it is rhyming slang for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a landlocked Himalayan country between India and China, with no sea coast.

clue.text: Short Disney movie about toys primarily—considered from the outset as brilliant

indicators.note: cut short means the film title loses its final letter
primarily points to the first letter of the word before it
about means surrounding, so the shortened title goes round the selected letter
the outset of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: Fantasia is Disney's 1940 animated film set to classical music
first letter of toys
first letter of considered

explanation.surface: A short Disney cartoon about toys was considered brilliant from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten the film to FANTASI, put the T inside it before its last letter, then add C.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic is informal praise meaning wonderful or excellent, a synonym for brilliant.

clue.text: Trainee carer working on bottom

blocks.note: a tender is one who tends or looks after, a carer at work
the foot of something is its bottom

explanation.surface: A care-worker apprentice is busy on someone's backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a novice or newcomer, originally a raw recruit, so a beginner still in training.

clue.text: Criticise performances on the radio—piano pieces

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: to knock is to criticise, and turns are stage performances

explanation.surface: A radio critic pans recitals of piano music.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a music-hall act; to knock is to run down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnes are dreamy night-pieces for piano, made famous by Chopin and Field.

clue.text: Perfect nice melody

blocks.note: fine and nice both mean pleasant or good
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A flawless, pleasant air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' reads as an adjective with the melody, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fine-tune is to make small adjustments until something works perfectly.

clue.text: Horror film about a submariner

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: The Omen is a 1976 horror film

explanation.surface: A scary movie concerning a man on a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novels, a famous fictional submariner.

clue.text: Recently put old end of beef in a pan

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
to pan a show is to slate it, criticise severely
O is the abbreviation for old
last letter of beef

explanation.surface: A cook recently put the last of some old beef into a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like a cooking pot; it is the verb meaning to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: As of late is an idiom meaning lately or in recent times.

clue.text: When entertaining royal a Commanding Officer bowed

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN
CO is the standard abbreviation for Commanding Officer

explanation.surface: An officer bowing as he hosts a member of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowed' suggests bending low before royalty; in music it means played with the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Arco is a musical direction telling string players to use the bow again rather than pluck.

clue.text: Beneath small organ that's supported from above

blocks.note: under means beneath
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a lung is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: Something lies below a little organ that hangs from a support.
explanation.definitionFit: An underslung part, such as a car chassis, hangs suspended beneath its supports rather than resting on them.

clue.text: Small wrap contains last of cucumber pickle

indicators.note: a thing that contains another holds it inside
the last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a cape is a wrap worn over the shoulders
last letter of cucumber

explanation.surface: A small sandwich wrap with some cucumber pickle inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' looks like the relish in the wrap; it means a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, and a pickle is an idiom for just such a fix.

clue.text: Take time to manage boats outside English docks

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to run a business is to manage it
cats is short for catamarans, twin-hulled boats
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: It takes a while to steer boats around English harbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docks' looks like harbours; it is the verb meaning to cut short. 'Take' only signals that time is collected.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock a tail is to cut it short, which is what truncating does.

clue.text: Expensive fur bought up front in transaction

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a sale is a commercial transaction
first letter of bought

explanation.surface: A costly fur coat was paid for in advance as part of a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' suggests paying in advance; it picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the prized dark pelt of a small Siberian marten, one of the costliest furs.

clue.text: Attack during match

blocks.note: a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: Someone has a seizure in the middle of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting fixture; it is the verb meaning to suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit in is to match one's surroundings, to blend or harmonise with them.

clue.text: Cardinal starts to examine Trappist's belief

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: a cardinal number, such as ten
first letters of examine and Trappist's

explanation.surface: A cardinal begins to investigate a Trappist monk's faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like the churchman; it is a counting number.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held as true, a synonym for belief.

clue.text: Sting at opening of Glasto has a dance

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a sting is a swindle, a con
first letter of Glasto
taken as written

explanation.surface: The singer Sting opens the Glastonbury festival and has a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting is the rock singer and Glasto the nickname of the Glastonbury music festival; cryptically a sting is a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed in a snaking single-file line.

clue.text: It's said the jellyfish is such a simple thing

blocks.note: surface reading: a remark about the jellyfish
setter's reading: a jellyfish has no brain at all, so it is literally a creature lacking one

explanation.surface: People say the jellyfish is an uncomplicated creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The informal word for an easy decision is read literally as a creature without a brain.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is an idiom for a decision so easy it needs no thought.

clue.text: Oriental flower festival

blocks.note: oriental means from the east, abbreviated to its compass letter
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A flower show with an Asian theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' in crosswords often means a river; here it is the bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian spring feast celebrating the resurrection.

clue.text: Pet's lead trips foot

indicators.note: something that trips stumbles and falls in a jumble, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A dog's leash catches someone's foot and sends them sprawling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' looks like the walker's foot; it means the base of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base or support on which a column or statue stands, its foot.
